title: Soft Horizon Buffer and Lease Negotiator — PRD Draft
body:
Overview:

This doc proposes an approach to letting customers make safer, more flexible commitments on Dedicated capacity by introducing two coordinated concepts: a Soft Horizon Buffer (SHB) — a pool of ephemeral compute headroom that can be shifted between commitments on a controlled schedule — and a Lease Negotiator subsystem that brokers short-lived, policy-bound resource loans between reservations.

Why this exists (problem framing):
- Customers want the predictability of reserved capacity but also need to handle unpredictable spikes (marketing spikes, model rollout hot paths, evaluation bursts).
- Pure burst-capacity models create noisy-neighbor risk and opaque billing/behavior for tenants.
- Heavy-handed preemption hurts latency SLAs and UX; pure isolation wastes GPU cycles.
- Existing burst-credit proposals at Redwood are numerous but often binary: either you get a credit or you don't. We need a smoother, auditable, reversible fabric that plays nicely with autoscaling and tenancy controls.

Goals (success criteria):
- Provide controlled short-term headroom customers can leverage without manual ops intervention.
- Avoid cliff preemptions: degrade latency gracefully when contention appears.
- Preserve tenant isolation guarantees: no silent theft of baseline reserved compute.
- Make economics transparent: predictable per-minute billing for ephemeral use, clear accounting back to reservation owners.
- Operationally simple: integrates with existing autoscaler signals, Console, and billing pipeline.

Non-goals:
- This is not a wholesale replacement for long-term reservations or the current burst-credit accounting model.
- We will not change the pricing model for base reservations in this iteration.

User stories:
- As an AI platform engineer (mid-market customer) I want my reserved pool to absorb occasional 3–7 minute spikes without coordination so my app's P95 latency stays within SLA.
- As a platform SRE I want soft-fail behaviors logged and surfaced in Console so I can correlate degradations to lease events.
- As a product manager I want a feature that lets Sales promise short-term capacity guarantees for launches without changing contracts.

Proposal (high level):
1) Soft Horizon Buffer (SHB)
   - SHB is a global or zone-local reservoir of fractional GPU headroom carved from overprovisioned physical hosts or idle warm pools.
   - SHB is not directly reserved; instead it is allocated as ephemeral leases to reservations via the Lease Negotiator.
   - SHB lifecycle: provisioned -> pooled -> loaned -> reclaimed -> replenished.
   - Policy knobs: max per-reservation borrow (% of reservation), borrow-duration cap (minutes), aggregate SHB caps per cluster/region, priority bands.

2) Lease Negotiator
   - A centralized (per-region) service that evaluates borrow requests from reservation controllers and issues short-lived leases backed by SHB capacity.
   - Inputs: reservation id, target concurrency, desired duration, priority tier, SLO fingerprint (latency target), and cost-preference (cheap vs low-latency).
   - Output: Lease token (opaque to caller) containing metadata: start/end, provisioned units, preemption-class, accounting code.
   - Enforcement: k8s/placement agent consumes lease token to provision/scale replicas; runtime enforces preemption class via tenant fences.

3) Shiftable Commitments (soft migration lanes)
   - Allow admins to define windows where a percentage of a reservation is marked as shiftable: e.g., "10% of pool A is shiftable Mon–Fri 00:00–06:00 UTC".
   - Shiftable capacity is lower priority to the original owner during their defined window; outside the window it behaves as regular reserved capacity.

Autoscaling interactions:
- Autoscaler will attempt to satisfy scaleups from: local reservation capacity -> cached KV/prefix reuse -> SHB via Lease Negotiator -> fallback to hosted API or lower-fidelity model variants.
- When requesting SHB, autoscaler includes SLO fingerprint and latency budget. Lease Negotiator uses these to choose appropriate SHB units (e.g., warm prewarmed slot vs opportunistic host).
- Backpressure: if SHB rejects the lease, autoscaler retries targeting degraded fidelity (smaller model or lower batch sizes) or queues the request based on configured latency hedges.

Isolation and graceful degradation model:
- Every SHB lease has a preemption_class: gentle, standard, emergency. Preemption_class indicates reclaim behavior: gentle reclaims allow KV checkpoints and progressively reduce concurrency; emergency reclaims are immediate and best-effort.
- We will introduce "isolation curtains": a runtime admission tag that marks requests as "protected" vs "best-effort". Protected requests are only served from baseline reservation or dedicated failover lanes; best-effort can use SHB.
- To avoid noisy neighbor surface, SHB loans carry tenant-scoped QoS ceilings (CPU/GPU fraction, memory) and runtime per-tenant fairness tokens.

Billing & accounting:
- SHB usage is metered per-minute and attributed to the borrower reservation. Billing tiers: premium (low-latency, higher $/min) vs opportunistic (cheaper but preemptible).
- Lease tokens contain accounting codes that feed into the existing cost attribution pipeline; Console will show minute-level SHB usage per route/model.

Operational concerns & safety guards:
- Reclamation speed vs data safety: define per-lease preemption grace (default 30s gentle -> 5s emergency).
- Observable traces: every lease lifecycle event emits to tracing and a structured audit log. Console will show active loans and projected reclaim risk.
- Limits and fraud: per-customer monthly cap on SHB minutes; anomaly detector alerts when consumption deviates from baseline patterns.

Technical design (implementation notes):
- Lease Negotiator is a new lightweight service: accepts gRPC requests, consults cluster SHB registry, and issues signed JWT lease tokens.
- SHB registry stores current physical headroom in etcd (sharded per-region). A reconciliation loop adjusts SHB based on host telemetry (idle GPU minutes, warm-pool hotness).
- Placement agent/Scaler integrates with existing kube-controller to consume lease tokens and attach node affinity + QoS annotations.
- Runtime enforcement hooks: modify request admission path to check for "protected" tag. If no protected capacity available, consult local cache and then fall back to consult Lease Negotiator (via autoscaler).

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Lease Negotiator outage: autoscaler should fallback to no-borrow strategy (deny SHB), and a degraded-mode flag surfaces in Console; avoid silent silent failover to hosted API unless explicitly configured.
- SHB overcommit: enforce strict aggregate caps and a conservative reconciliation frequency (e.g., 30s) to avoid oversubscription oscillations.
- Billing misattribution: double-write prevention on lease issuance (idempotency tokens).

Console UX & controls:
- New Console page: "Soft Horizon" showing regional SHB pool, active leases, reclaim risk heatmap, and per-reservation borrow history.
- Admin controls: configure per-reservation borrow policies, set monthly SHB caps, mark shiftable windows, and set default preemption_class.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (canary): implement Lease Negotiator and SHB registry in a single region, enable for internal beta customers only. Metrics: lease issuance latency <100ms, no production P99 regressions.
- Phase 1: enable autoscaler integration for a subset of customers (by opt-in flag). Add Console visibility.
- Phase 2: expand to 3 regions, introduce billing pipeline hooks.
- Phase 3: GA with policy templates and SRE playbook.

SRE playbook (draft):
- If reclaim storms observed: 1) pause new lease issuance, 2) increase reconciliation interval, 3) throttle opportunistic preemptible class, 4) notify affected customers via Console banner.
- If billing spike: freeze SHB usage for offending reservation and trigger manual review.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How granular should SHB units be? full-GPU minutes vs fractional slices? Fractional is more efficient but adds scheduling complexity.
- Where do we draw the line between shiftable commitments and explicit reseller contracts?
- Preemption semantics: can we offer soft-evacuation for KV-backed inferences? What is the expected customer code change surface?
- Accounting for model fidelity changes: if autoscaler degrades model to avoid lease denial, should the billing metric be tied to tokens served or compute-minutes consumed?

Next steps / action items:
- RFC: Julian to draft an internal RFC outlining Lease Negotiator API by 2025-11-14.
- Prototype: Infra to sketch SHB registry prototype and simulation harness (Connor).
- Customer discovery: PM to run 3 deep-dive interviews with mid-market customers who asked for launch guarantees (María).
- Wireframes: UX to produce Console mockups for SHB page.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally exploratory; looking for feedback on the policy surface and operational boundaries. Please annotate with use cases where this either helps or complicates your current workflows.

Quick links referenced in doc:
- Jira: JIRA-DEDICATED-2013 (lease-negotiator epic)
- RFC draft placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/331

TODOs inline:

- [ ] Confirm billing model and necessary backend invoice fields with Finance.

----
Author notes (quick):
- Focus on predictability and observability over squeezing marginal cost improvements. Customers value clear tradeoffs.
- Keep the Lease Negotiator API deliberately narrow so teams can iterate on reclaim semantics.
- This design aims to reduce the number of abrupt evictions and give product/ops teams more levers to promise capacity without overcommitting hosts.
